- When sentiment is strongly bullish (≥0.67) and news volume is high, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- After a sharp price spike (≥5% from prior period), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +3% above prior peak for 2–3 periods.
- If sentiment turns bearish (≤0.33) and news volume drops to 0–2, model overcorrects downward; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast to avoid premature bottoming.
- Model underestimates when sentiment is volatile (rapid changes >0.33) and news volume is low; adjust upward by 0.5–1.5% to compensate for lag.
- Mean reversion bias: if price is above 3σ from 30-day moving average, reduce forecast by 0.5–1.5% per period until reversion.
- For 30-day horizon, model often misses late-period sentiment shifts; apply a 1–2% upward adjustment if sentiment turns bullish in last 3–5 days.
